profile.headline: Retired Software Engineer
profile.summary:
I am retired from a 40-year career in computer graphics.  Some of the highlights have been:
- Contributing to 3D special effects software used in blockbuster movies.
- Contributing to musculoskeletal modeling software used to help people overcome walking disorders.
- Contributing to surgical simulation software used to train medics and nurses.
- Creating 3D map editing software used to create an accurate model of planet Earth.

Now I'm busy with:
- Numerous DIY projects on our 100 year old house.
- Spending time with my familiy... especially the grandchildren.
- Writing a TV screenplay (if you are a producer of premium sci-fi TV, please contact me!).
- Cooking, Excercising, and hanging out with friends!

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Creator of WebScape, a 3D map editor used by hundreds of people within HERE.

• Architect and lead engineer of multiple front-end tools and batch pipelines for extracting 3D map features (poles, trees, windows, terrain) from source data (lidar point clouds, street-level & satellite imagery). Highlights include a web tool for labeling 3D point clouds (somewhat like a Photoshop for point clouds), and a patented process for extracting windows from street-level imagery.

positions.title: Lead Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Lead inventor of US Patent 10,955,256 - Mapping system and method for applying texture to visual representations of buildings.

• Added a variety of features to Here’s core 3D map editor (overpass modeling, aerial mesh display, street-level imagery display, workflow-specific user interfaces).

• Created interactive tools to visualize and improve the quality of HERE's 3D map of the world using JavaScript and C++.

positions.title: Founder and Engineer
positions.description:
• iPhone contract programming on a team developing a distributed, social marketing platform.

• Co-creator and engineer of Bon Mot!, an original word game for the iPhone and iPod touch.

positions.title: Sr. Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Architect of the next generation of Write Brothers' flagship product, Movie Magic Screenwriter. Screenwriter is a specialized word processor for film, television, and stage writers. This project involved a ground-up design and implementation based on the Cocoa Advanced Text framework from Apple and using the open-source Cocotron project to port from Mac to Windows.

• Architect and lead engineer of Word Menu, an English language dictionary organized into a hierarchy of categories and employing modern user-interface techniques to quickly browse and search the content.

• Added a variety of features to StoryView 2.0, a visual outlining tool for writers.  This project involved a team of four engineers using a formal team methodology based on the software Capability Maturity Model.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Ported MusculoGraphics' flagship product, SIMM (Software for Interactive Musculoskeletal Modeling) from SGI Irix/GL to MS-Windows/OpenGL, and added several major features for the release of version 2.0 including: muscle wrapping, bone deformation, and motion capture support.

* Lead programer for LTS (Limb Trauma Simulator), a multi-threaded realtime surgical simulator consisting of a PC controlling two Sensable Phantom force-feedback devices for spatial input and haptic output, and an SGI Octane for stereoscopic realtime 3D display.  I wrote most of the code and shared design responsibilities with one other engineer.  I worked on all aspects of the simulator including the overall architecture, graphics engine, haptic force feedback, and TCP/IP-based communication between the graphics and haptics computers.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Co-authored a cross-platform (Mac, Win32, Unix), object-oriented application framework for the Electric Image 3D modeller. 

• Designed and implemented skeletal and free-form deformation tools based on papers presented at Siggraph.

• Designed and implemented Renderama, Electric Image's distributed rendering system. This involved a client-server architecture using TCP/IP and AppleTalk protocols.

• Designed and implemented spatial deformation tools for Electric Image Animation System 2. This feature went on to receive excellent reviews in MacWEEK 08.01.94 (page 58).

• Implemented video and audio support in EIAS 2 including creation and playback of QuickTime movies as well as capture, display, manipulation, and playback of 8-bit, 2 channel audio.

• Various projects including: porting EI's rendering engine to PowerMac, custom UI widgets, and more...

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Designed, coded and documented two C++ class libraries -- one to provide generic container classes, memory management and I/O, another to provide a portable UI application framework. Together these libraries comprise 76 C++ classes built upon the Win32 and Mac OS Toolbox APIs. Additionally I ported the container class library to Unix System V and Mach platforms. Screenplay Systems has shipped at least three applications based on these libraries.

• Worked on Movie Magic Budgeting II, Screenplay Systems' 2nd-generation movie budgeting application. MMB is a single-user, hyperlinked spreadsheet application complete with a byte-compiled macro language. MMB makes use of the class libraries mentioned above to target both Mac OS and Windows with one set of source code.

patents.title: Mapping system and method for applying texture to visual representations of buildings
patents.description: A mapping system, method and computer program product are provided to apply texture, such as windows and doors, to the visual representation of a plurality of buildings. In the context of a method, images of each of a plurality of buildings are analyzed to detect building texture for one or more faces of the buildings. A representation of the building texture is spread to visual representations of one or more faces of a respective building that do not have a detected texture. The building texture may be spread from another face of the same building that has detected texture and is of a corresponding size to the face of the building without detected texture. Or, the building texture may be spread from a face of a neighboring building has a detected texture and is of a corresponding size to the face of the building without detected texture.
